changes: Worlds take much less memory: blocks are now stored chunk by chunk, so a new 1280 x 1280 world needs about 120 MB instead of 300 MB, and there's no longer a limit of 256 kinds of block
New worlds have biomes (choose "Biomes" when you make a world; older worlds stay as they were): Woods, Plains, Meadows, Taiga, Snowy lands, Deserts, Badlands and Swamps
Plains: flat, open grassland with flowers and a lone tree here and there
Meadows: gently rolling grass packed with flowers of every colour (the place to find dyes), with a few more trees than the plains
Taiga: thick Fir forests on ordinary grass, between the woods and the snowy lands, so the cold comes on gradually
Deserts: rolling sand dunes dotted with Palm trees, with Sandstone under the sand
Badlands: steep hills striped with coloured Terracotta (plain, orange, yellow, red, white and pink), next to the deserts: dig them for coloured terracotta without any dye
Snowy lands: Snowy Grass, pointed Fir trees, and seas and lakes frozen over with Ice
Swamps: low, flat, boggy land with shallow muddy pools, lots of clay, Willow trees with drooping leaves, and Mud and Peat under the grass
New blocks: Sandstone, Snowy Grass, Ice and Swamp Grass (digging up any grass gives Dirt; hoes till it and flowers plant on it)
New water picture: ripples, and a softer outline so seas and lakes no longer look like a grid
New looks for the terracottas, Sand, Sandstone, Clay, Fireclay, Leaves, the grass side, the Crafting Bench and the Cutter
Swamp Grass has its own picture (murky green with darker patches, and moss hanging over the side), and Snowy Grass has a snowy side

Grass and leaves take on the colour of the climate they grow in, fading smoothly from biome to biome: bluer near the snow, yellower near deserts, murkier in swamps, brighter in plains (Biome worlds only)

New wood: Fir, from the snowy lands' trees. Fir Log, Stripped Fir Log, Fir Planks (they make Sticks, Crafting Benches and Cutters, and cut into slabs and stairs like any planks) and Fir Leaves (the leaf picture, coloured a darker blue-green on top of the climate colour); logs and planks burn in the Kiln
The original wood is now called Oak: Oak Log, Stripped Oak Log, Oak Planks and Oak Leaves

New wood: Palm, from the desert's trees, and Willow, from the swamp's. Each has a Log, Stripped Log, Planks (Sticks, Crafting Benches and Cutters, slabs and stairs) and Leaves in their own colour; logs and planks burn in the Kiln
Dates: breaking Palm Leaves sometimes drops Dates, a food you can only find in the desert

Desert stone: Sandstone Bricks and Chiseled Sandstone (Sandstone at the Crafting Bench, with a pickaxe), and Smooth Sandstone (Sandstone fired in the Kiln). Sandstone and its blocks now need a pickaxe, and cut into slabs and stairs
Mud: the swamp's ground. Dig it with a shovel (by hand you get Mud Pieces); the Kiln fires it into Mud Bricks, a new building block
Peat: found under the swamp's mud. It's the best Kiln fuel: one Peat smelts 8 things (a log only smelts 4)
New worlds are four times bigger: 1280 x 1280 blocks instead of 640 x 640 (worlds you already have stay the size they are)
The main menu has a panorama: a view of this update's new biomes (badlands, palms, swamp and taiga) slowly turns behind the title
Fixed Zombies and Grr Angry hitting you through walls, floors and ceilings (from a cave under you, say)
The Foundry's Furnace has a Fireclay Bricks top and a new brown front
The Crafting Bench no longer lists the deep stone blocks, which aren't in the game yet

New block: the Cutter (3 Planks + a Copper Brick at the Crafting Bench), half a block tall with a spinning saw blade on top, cuts blocks into pieces, slabs and stairs; the Crafting Bench is just for crafting now

title: Pack & Plate
changes: Armor: helmets, chestplates, leggings and boots in leather, copper, iron, bronite, rosium and steel; they soak up hits and wear out
Backpacks (5 to 40 more slots) and Utility Belts (more offhand slots and 2 to 7 more tool slots), worn on your back and waist
A bigger survival inventory: 10 Pockets, tool slots that pick the right tool for you, and an offhand (R picks, F swaps, right-click uses it)
The inventory is laid out side by side: your slots on the left, crafting on the right, the same in the web and desktop editions
Ores: Copper, Iron, Tin and Gold, each needing a good enough pickaxe
Fireclay, its bricks and blocks, and the Foundry, which melts ore Chunks into Bricks and mixes alloys: Bronite, Rosium and Steel
Metal tools in copper, iron, bronite, rosium and steel
Tools wear out with use and break; a bar shows how much is left
Bedrock lines the bottom of the world
Sand, Gravel and Dirt fall when there's nothing under them
Plays multiplayer with web version Beta 0.1.0.0
Fixed see-through walls of water showing inside the sea near the edge of the world
Plays multiplayer with web version Alpha 0.0.9.5
Cows: they wander and graze on grass, and happy cows show pink hearts
Happy cows with room around them may have a calf, which follows the grown-ups and grows up after a while
Crowded cows don't mate, and once a chunk has 8 cows (calves and fat cows count) none of them breed
Feed a cow Grain to fatten it up: the more it has been fed, the more Raw Meat it drops
Cows with more room grow a bigger hide and drop more Leather
Cook Raw Meat into Cooked Meat in the kiln
Crops grow at random: some plants get ahead and some lag a little, so a field doesn't all ripen at once
Render distance slider in Settings (4 to 32 chunks): land past it isn't drawn and fades into the haze
Only the chunks within your render distance are built, so worlds load faster
Mobs only keep going within the render distance; cows further away wait where they are
Mobs now wait while you're paused, like the rest of the world
Plays multiplayer with web version Alpha 0.0.9.4
The world is drawn in 32x32x32 groups of chunks: far fewer pieces to draw each frame, so the game spends much less time on every frame
Chunks are still built as 16x16x16 cubes, so breaking and placing blocks stays fast
The world loads one 32x32x32 group at a time, nearest first
Chunks are now 16x16x16 cubes, stacked 12 high, instead of tall 16x16 columns
Digging, building, water and torches rebuild only the cubes around them, so changing a block is about 8 times faster
Empty sky isn't built at all, and caves and hilltops out of view are skipped on their own
Tools in your hand are 50% bigger, and the Hoe is turned the right way round
Your hand shows the whole arm now, running right off the edge of the screen
Fixed the arm jittering when you sprint-jump
Clay Balls dry into Bricks in 2 minutes instead of 5
New recipe: 4 Clay Balls pack back into a Clay block
Dirt and Gravel have swapped sounds
Leaves only drop themselves when mined with a Hoe; anything else just has the 1 in 5 chance of a Stick
The GUI is one size smaller, still in whole pixels
Farming! Right-click Grass or Dirt with a Hoe to till it into soil (tilling Grass sometimes turns up Grain Seeds)
Plant Grain Seeds on tilled soil; Grain grows through 8 stages, and ripe Grain gives Grain plus 1-2 seeds
Soil joined to water (through other tilled soil, up to 5 blocks away) is wet and grows Grain twice as fast
Bone Ash fertilizes soil for 2 harvests and makes Grain grow faster still
Dry tilled soil with nothing planted turns back into Dirt after a few minutes
Grain -> Flour by hand, Flour -> Bread in the Kiln; Bread is food
The Zombie is the night mob now, taking over from Grr Angry
New mob: the Skeleton comes out in the dark, keeps its distance and throws Rocks at you. It burns in daylight and drops Bones
New mob: the Gloomling lives deep underground in the pitch dark and snuffs out burning torches. It fades away if you come near holding a lit torch
Defeat a Gloomling to get a Gloom Wisp
Bones smelt into Bone Ash in the Kiln
White Dye is now made from Bone Ash, and Black Dye from a Gloom Wisp
The arrow keys look around too, as a backup for laptops
Fixed looking around with the mouse on PCs where the mouse wouldn't turn the camera
Slabs, stairs, quarters and pieces now show as little 3D models in the inventory, as sharp as full blocks
Dropped blocks, slabs, stairs, pieces and torches are now little 3D models instead of flat pictures
Tools are held properly: gripped near the end of the handle and turned side-on, so you swing with the head, not the flat
Tools in your hand are 1 pixel thick, for a little depth
Blocks in your inventory, hotbar and recipes show as little 3D cubes, including the kiln (with its opening); torches show as a small 3D stick
The + on blocks with other forms is smaller, neatly centred and tucked into the slot's bottom-right corner
Menus and the hotbar scale with your screen's display scaling by a whole number (150% makes them twice as big), so every pixel stays even

title: Shape & Shade
changes: Skin menu: paint your own player skin, with a turning 3D preview
Your hand now wears your skin
New player figure with elbows and knees
Other players look like players in their own skin, holding their items
New letters, numbers and symbols
Plays multiplayer with web version Alpha 0.0.7.0
Holding a torch now lights up the area around you, so you can see in dark caves and at night
Plays multiplayer with web version Alpha 0.0.6.1

title: Brick & Bloom
changes: Terracotta, Chiseled Terracotta and Bricks in 12 colours
Flowers grow in small patches on grass; pick them and plant them again
12 Dyes from flowers, Burnt Torches and Rocks, plus mixing for more colours
Plays multiplayer with web version Alpha 0.0.6.0
Cubeland as a desktop program for Windows, made in Godot, with the same version number as the web game
Plays multiplayer with the web version: host or join with the same 5-letter codes
Uses your font and menu pictures, like the web version
